title: chore(client): declare and assert the Node engine floor across every client build path; register the two review findings in SPRINTS.md
intent: PR #279 raises @vitejs/plugin-vue to 6.0.8, whose declared engine is ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0 (up from ^18.0.0 || >=20.0.0). The repo had no machine-readable Node floor anywhere: packages/client/package.json had no engines field, and there is no .nvmrc, .node-version, or .npmrc. Every client build path resolved Node from a bare major (setup-node 20, ARG NODE_VERSION=20), which satisfies the new floor today only because floating tags resolve upward. This patch declares the floor once and asserts it at every build entry point, so a downward change or a stale cached base image fails with a named error instead of an opaque Vite/ESM failure. It does not change the resolved Node version on any current build path.

diff_articulation.what_changed: packages/client/package.json gains engines.node = '^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0', the single declared source of truth, mirroring @vitejs/plugin-vue 6.x. packages/client/.nvmrc (new) pins 20.19.0 for local shells. The four client Dockerfiles (docker/client/Dockerfile, .production, .railway, and packages/client/Dockerfile - the last of which is live via packages/client/railway.json dockerfilePath) each gain one RUN node -e assertion immediately after the builder FROM, exiting 1 with a named message when the base image is below the floor. client_lint_build.yml changes node-version from the bare major 20 to the range '^20.19.0' - still resolving the newest 20.x so security patches land, but now failing at setup-node rather than mid-build if the floor is ever unmet. containers.yml, docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.production.yml and .env.example keep NODE_VERSION=20 (which floats above the floor) and gain comments naming the floor and its source; docker-compose.yml's stale '20+ required for Vite 5' comment is corrected. SPRINTS.md: MAINT-DEFER-004 gains two dated addenda - an R-11 scope extension recording that the withheld SG_SPEC_TOKEN also kills the container lane (API image builds first in containers/core_ci/proxy_parity/proxy_adaptive, so the client image is never reached and a client-only Dependabot PR has zero container coverage), and a classification of #279 itself as a Tranche C client major toolchain bump requiring consolidated-PR handling. New MAINT-DEFER-005 registers the GitHub Actions Node-20 runtime deprecation with a measured pin inventory (174 pins / 54 workflow files), restore trigger, done-condition, and a sequencing note against a 53-file sweep while CI-RED-021 is OPEN. Header Last updated 2026-08-10 -> 2026-08-17. REVIEW HARDENING: (a) the four inline `node -e` guards are replaced by one scripts/check-node-engine.mjs that READS engines.node instead of restating it, so the Dockerfiles cannot drift from the manifest or from each other; each now COPYs the script next to package.json and runs it before `npm ci`, preserving the fail-fast property. (b) The declared floor was wrong for the tree it describes: @supabase/supabase-js@2.112.3 and its five sibling packages are non-optional PRODUCTION dependencies declaring engines.node >=22.0.0, so the previous floor's ^20.19.0 lane admitted a runtime those dependencies reject - and containers.yml, both compose files, .env.example and all four Dockerfile ARG defaults sat on exactly that lane. The floor is now >=22.12.0 and every NODE_VERSION default moves 20 -> 22. (c) The rationale repeated in all those comments, 'required by @vitejs/plugin-vue 6.x', was false: the installed plugin-vue is 5.2.4 with engines ^18.0.0 || >=20.0.0. Comments now point at the manifest rather than restating a range or a reason. (d) A new spec asserts the floor against the lockfile and against every Node pin that no runtime guard covers. FOLLOW-UP REVIEW: (a) satisfiesClause implemented real caret semantics - ^0.2.3 is >=0.2.3 <0.3.0, not 'any 0.x'. Unreachable for a Node engine range, but the helper is exported and unit-tested, so it implements the rule rather than the convenient approximation. (b) The drift spec stripped YAML comments before scanning, so a commented-out `# node-version: 18` is dead text rather than something the gate reads. (c) The dependency scan previously skipped any engines.node range that was not a tidy single-lane '>=x' - 210 checked, 11 skipped - which quietly narrowed 'every dependency' into 'every dependency with convenient syntax'. It now derives the lowest version any lane could accept and skips only genuinely unconstrained ranges; the test name says what it does. (d) containers.yml now builds packages/client/Dockerfile with packages/client as the context, which is the entry point Railway actually uses and which no CI job covered. (e) railway.json watchPatterns gained scripts/** and package-lock.json. (f) The stale yourorg/ OCI source label in Dockerfile.production corrected. (g) The script header now records why npm engine-strict is not enabled.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: No existing mechanism encodes a Node floor for this workspace - no engines field, no .nvmrc, no .npmrc, no CI assertion - so nothing today would catch a regression to Node 18 or 20.9 except an opaque downstream build failure. The Dockerfile assertion is not redundant with the workflow change: four of the five client-image call sites (core_ci.yml:181, proxy_parity.yml:44, proxy_adaptive.yml:43, publish-images.yml:159) pass no NODE_VERSION build-arg at all and silently inherit the Dockerfile ARG default, so a workflow-only fix would leave them uncovered. The ledger additions are not redundant with R-11: R-11 scopes the constraint to api-verify only and does not record the container-lane consequence, and no repo document tracked the Actions runtime deprecation at all (grep over SPRINTS.md and docs/ci/ returned nothing).

files.intent: Single derived engine-floor guard, replacing four hand-written inline copies.
files.behavior_change: Reads engines.node from packages/client/package.json and validates process.versions.node against it. Fails closed on an unreadable manifest, an absent engines.node, or a semver clause form it does not implement - it throws rather than guessing, because a silently mis-parsed range is worse than no check. Also exposed as `npm run check:node`.

files.intent: Keep every unguarded Node pin, and the declared floor itself, consistent with the dependency tree.
files.behavior_change: Six assertions: the floor is declared; no non-optional dependency requires more Node than the floor admits; .nvmrc, every NODE_VERSION default and every workflow node-version can satisfy it; and no Dockerfile restates the range by hand. The dependency assertion reproduces the defect this change fixes - against the previous floor it fails with the six @supabase packages.

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: Build-time guard only; no application code, no runtime behavior, and no resolved-version change on any current build path. The single non-comment functional edit outside the guards is client_lint_build.yml node-version 20 -> ^20.19.0, which resolves to the same Node release today. Deliberately NOT done: hard-pinning NODE_VERSION to the literal floor 20.19.0, which would have moved every image from the newest 20.x down to an older patch level and dropped security fixes for no safety gain. Ledger additions are documentation only and mint no new CI-RED id.
